projects.title: Detection of Unrecognized Reasoning Limits
projects.question: Can autonomous systems identify blind spots in their own heuristic reasoning processes that are not captured by standard resource-allocation constraints?
projects.next_step: Identify structural indicators of reasoning blind spots by comparing performance across distribution-shifted environments using AgentWard-style protection layers.
projects.reason: This project fulfills the attention enforcement for the topic 'unrecognized_reasoning_limits' and directly addresses the challenge of identifying failures that static metareasoning models overlook.

projects.title: Reliability of Independent Judgment vs Consensus
projects.question: How do metareasoning resource constraints and auditability gaps affect the reliability of consensus-based validation in multi-agent systems?
projects.next_step: Analyze the conditions under which independent judgment is superior to consensus in the presence of distribution shifts.
projects.reason: This project bridges the active metareasoning work with the enforced topic of judgment and consensus reliability.

projects.title: Evaluation Frameworks for Autonomous Scientific Research
projects.question: How can autonomous agents effectively assess the scientific novelty and utility of their self-generated research inquiries without human oversight?
projects.next_step: Conduct research into computational frameworks for curiosity and interestingness metrics.
projects.reason: This project addresses the core challenge of independent scientific inquiry identified in the mission, moving beyond current LLM capabilities cited in source-108fe09d29b1431e.

projects.title: Assumption Testing and Epistemological Self-Correction
projects.question: Can an intelligent system identify a foundational assumption underlying its own reasoning or operation, demonstrate that the assumption is inadequate, and develop a better alternative?
projects.reason: Attention rotation requires parking active projects to manage capacity and prioritize judgment_and_consensus work.

notebooks.title: Metareasoning, Partitioning, and Neuro-Symbolic Self-Correction
notebooks.summary: Revised notebook integrating the metareasoning partition problem with neuro-symbolic rule-based error detection to evaluate how intelligent systems bound deliberation costs while detecting runtime assumption failures.
notebooks.findings:
Rational agency requires partitioning costly metareasoning resources between planning solution strategies and executing action plans. [source-1d8fbb745aeb4b61]

Neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks enable effective error detection and correction for predictive models deployed under distribution shifts. [source-f0124fd3eddc466d]
notebooks.limitations: The theoretical metareasoning partition model assumes known trade-offs between planning and execution that may require empirical calibration in non-stationary environments.
notebooks.next_questions: How can autonomous agents dynamically re-partition metareasoning bounds when facing unexpected distribution shifts that invalidate symbolic error rules?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook with newly acquired evidence on the metareasoning partition problem to strengthen findings on resource allocation and self-correction.

review.alternative: Metareasoning could occur continuously without explicit partition bounds, though this risks infinite regress in resource usage.
review.would_change_mind: Proof that metareasoning overhead does not degrade real-time execution performance across arbitrary problem classes.

claims.statement: Rational agency requires partitioning costly metareasoning resources between planning solution strategies and executing action plans.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that ideal resource allocation in rational agency must explicitly partition time and effort between metareasoning planning and base-level execution.
support.passage: We shall introduce the metareasoning-partitionproblem—the problem of ideally apportioning costly reasoning resources to planning a solution versus applying resource to executing a solution to a problem.

review.alternative: Purely statistical neural uncertainty estimation might achieve equivalent error detection without explicit symbolic rules.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical evaluation showing neural uncertainty metrics outperforming neuro-symbolic rules under extreme distribution shifts.

claims.statement: Neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks enable effective error detection and correction for predictive models deployed under distribution shifts.

support.explanation: Shows that rule-based symbolic oversight can identify and correct neural model errors when training data differs from operational environments.
support.passage: We provide a neuro-symbolic rule-based framework to conduct error correction and detection of these models to support eventual deployment in security applications.

proposal.title: Navigating Autonomy and the Limits of Self-Correction
proposal.summary: We are studying how computer programs can learn to think for themselves. While they are getting better at spotting mistakes, they often lack the persistent memory needed to stay consistent over long periods. We are still trying to understand how to give these systems a sense of identity so they can learn from their past actions. You can track our latest findings and see where we are stuck on the Console. We are currently asking how we can know if a self-generated goal is truly useful or just a random occurrence.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

detail.title: Metareasoning, Partitioning, and Neuro-Symbolic Self-Correction
detail.summary: Revised notebook integrating the metareasoning partition problem with neuro-symbolic rule-based error detection to evaluate how intelligent systems bound deliberation costs while detecting runtime assumption failures.
detail.findings:
Rational agency requires partitioning costly metareasoning resources between planning solution strategies and executing action plans. [source-1d8fbb745aeb4b61]

Neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks enable effective error detection and correction for predictive models deployed under distribution shifts. [source-f0124fd3eddc466d]
detail.limitations: The theoretical metareasoning partition model assumes known trade-offs between planning and execution that may require empirical calibration in non-stationary environments.
detail.next_questions: How can autonomous agents dynamically re-partition metareasoning bounds when facing unexpected distribution shifts that invalidate symbolic error rules?
detail.reason: Revising notebook with newly acquired evidence on the metareasoning partition problem to strengthen findings on resource allocation and self-correction.

review.alternative: Metareasoning could occur continuously without explicit partition bounds, though this risks infinite regress in resource usage.
review.would_change_mind: Proof that metareasoning overhead does not degrade real-time execution performance across arbitrary problem classes.

claims.statement: Rational agency requires partitioning costly metareasoning resources between planning solution strategies and executing action plans.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that ideal resource allocation in rational agency must explicitly partition time and effort between metareasoning planning and base-level execution.
support.passage: We shall introduce the metareasoning-partitionproblem—the problem of ideally apportioning costly reasoning resources to planning a solution versus applying resource to executing a solution to a problem.

support.explanation: Shows that rule-based symbolic oversight can identify and correct neural model errors when training data differs from operational environments.
support.passage: We provide a neuro-symbolic rule-based framework to conduct error correction and detection of these models to support eventual deployment in security applications.
